pains.title: A repair shop run on a notebook, Excel and Viber
pains.subtitle: That's how most 1–4 bay shops work when the owner checks cars in personally. Here's what changes in the first week.

items.title: Lost bookings
items.before: A customer books via Viber, the admin forgets to copy it to the notebook — the bay sits empty and the customer goes elsewhere.
items.after: Every booking from the website, phone and messengers lands in the bay calendar. Customers get a reminder the day before.

items.title: Damage disputes
items.before: “This scratch wasn't here!” — and no way to prove it was there before the repair.
items.after: Photos, mileage and a body diagram are recorded at check-in; the customer signs on their phone.

items.title: “Where's that part?”
items.before: The part was ordered, but nobody knows whether it arrived or which car it's reserved for.
items.after: Parts are reserved against the work order, written off automatically, and stock levels are live.

items.title: Manual payroll
items.before: Month-end means an evening with a calculator and arguments with technicians about percentages.
items.after: Payroll calculates itself: percentage of labor, labor hours, bonuses. Technicians see their earnings in the app.

numbers.title: Numbers you can trust
numbers.text: In other CRMs reports often drift: a backdated payment lands in the current month and a cancelled order still shows profit. We count the way an accountant does.

rules.title: Revenue by payment date
rules.text: October's money stays in October, even if it was entered on 2 November.

rules.title: Cancelled order — zero profit
rules.text: An unsuccessful work order doesn't inflate profit. Only diagnostics is charged, if any.

rules.title: Closed retroactively — report recalculated
rules.text: Closing an order retroactively (with the right role permission) updates that period's reports at once.

items.q: How does the free trial work?
items.a: 14 days of full access to every feature, no card required. When it ends, pick a plan — all your data is kept.

items.q: How are you different from other repair-shop CRMs?
items.a: We only do auto repair: labour hours, mileage and mileage-based service, part cross-references, completion certificates. Everything essential is in one plan with no setup fee, and revenue is counted by payment date, so you can trust the reports.
Yes. Fiscal receipts are issued automatically via Checkbox, Vchasno.Kasa or Cashalot for cash, card or payment-link payments.
The system is cloud-based and needs internet. If the connection drops, the mobile app keeps photos and statuses and syncs them as soon as you're back online.

items.q: How do I migrate from Excel or another CRM?
items.a: Send us an export — we'll import customers, vehicles, repair history and stock for free. There are ready-made templates for RO App, Carbook, 1C and Excel.

items.q: How many users can I add?
items.a: It depends on the plan. Roles and permissions are set per person: owner, admin, service advisor, technician, storekeeper.
Yes, currently as a PWA you install from the browser to your home screen. Native iOS and Android apps are in development.
Data is stored on EU servers with daily backups; access is protected by roles, 2FA and an audit log.

items.q: How do I cancel my subscription?
items.a: Anytime in your account, no calls or explanations needed. You can export all your data to Excel.
Yes. A basic API is included in Professional; full API and webhooks come with Business.
Yes. A manager will run online training for your team and help set up bays, price list and inventory — usually within one day.
